definitions.explanation: Originally a duel between two mounted warriors, now used figuratively to describe a direct contest or showdown between two rivals, teams, or candidates.

examples.japanese: ⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一騎打|いっきう}ちになった。
examples.english: It came down to a showdown between the two.

examples.japanese: ⟦{選挙|せんきょ}→選挙：03303_senkyo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{与党|よとう}→与党：05241_yotou⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{野党|やとう}→野党：02438_yatou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一騎打|いっきう}ちだった。
examples.english: The election was a head-to-head contest between the ruling and opposition parties.

examples.japanese: ⟦{決勝|けっしょう}→決勝：04742_kesshou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{昨年|さくねん}→昨年：10433_sakunen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦チャンピオン→チャンピオン：19399_chanpion⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一騎打|いっきう}ち⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{最後|さいご}→最後：01413_saigo⟧⟦まで→まで：00490_made⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{離|はな}せなかった→離す：19372_hanasu⟧。
examples.english: The final was a one-on-one battle with last year's champion, and I couldn't take my eyes off it until the end.

notes:
{一騎打|いっきう}ち originally referred to single combat between mounted warriors ({騎|き} means "mounted rider") in medieval Japan. Today it is used almost entirely in its figurative sense.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一騎打|いっきう}ち⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ (come down to a showdown)
- {一騎打|いっきう}ち⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{演|えん}じる→演じる：13330_enjiru⟧ (put on a one-on-one battle)
- ⟦{事実上|じじつじょう}→事実上：11419_jijitsujou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一騎打|いっきう}ち (a de facto showdown)

USAGE:
- Very common in politics (⟦{選挙|せんきょ}→選挙：03303_senkyo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一騎打|いっきう}ち) and sports reporting
- Always implies exactly two competitors, not a broader contest
- Carries a dramatic, high-stakes nuance
